title: Giving the model knowledge
hook: Prompt, RAG, tools, or fine-tuning. Four different problems that get mixed up.
inPlainWords: Four different gaps get confused. Missing instructions need a prompt. Missing facts need retrieval (RAG). Missing live data or actions need tools. A missing style or narrow skill needs fine-tuning.

useCase.title: Answer "What is your return policy for opened electronics?"
useCase.story: The policy lives in 40 documents and changes every month. The bot must give the current answer with a source, not last year's.

approaches.name: Ask the model directly
approaches.what: Rely on what the model remembers from training.
approaches.example: "What is ShopEase's return window?" gets an invented number.

approaches.name: Paste everything in the prompt
approaches.what: Put the whole document into every request (long context).
approaches.avoidWhen: Hundreds of pages. It is slow, costly, and details get lost.

approaches.name: RAG: look up, then answer
approaches.what: Search your documents first, and hand only the relevant parts to the model.
approaches.greatWhen: Knowledge is large or changing, and you need citations.
approaches.avoidWhen: The knowledge is tiny and fits comfortably in one prompt.
approaches.example: Find the electronics-returns paragraph, then answer with a link to it.

approaches.name: Fine-tuning
approaches.what: Train the model further on your examples so its behavior changes.
approaches.greatWhen: A consistent voice, format, or narrow skill.
approaches.example: Train the bot to always answer in ShopEase's voice.

approaches.name: Tools and API lookups
approaches.what: The model asks your software for live data or to take an action.
approaches.avoidWhen: Static policy text. Use RAG for that.
approaches.example: Look up the shipping status of order 48213.

challenge.question: Policy text changes monthly and answers must be current, with a source. What is the best approach?

options.why: Update a document and the next answer is current. No retraining, and you can cite the source.

options.text: Fine-tune the model on the policy
options.why: It bakes in facts that will go stale, and you cannot point to where it learned them.
It does not know your policy. It will guess.

options.text: Paste all 40 documents into every prompt
options.why: Works at small scale, but it is slow and costly, and details get lost.

bestCase.title: RAG for facts, tools for live data, fine-tuning only for style
bestCase.example: The policy is updated on Monday. On Tuesday a customer asks about opened electronics. The bot finds the new paragraph and answers: 14 days, 10% restocking fee, with a link to the Returns Policy.

worstCase.title: Fine-tuning facts into the model
worstCase.example: You fine-tune on last year's policy. The bot now confidently quotes the old 30-day window, you cannot tell where it learned that, and fixing it means training again.

steps.label: Search your documents
steps.goes: It finds the two most relevant policy paragraphs.
steps.goesWrong: There is no search. The model answers from memory and says "30 days", which was last year's rule.

steps.label: Build the prompt
steps.goes: Question plus passages: "Answer only using these passages."

steps.label: Language model
steps.goes: It writes a short answer from the passages.

steps.label: Answer with source
steps.goes: The answer is shown with a link to the policy.

takeaway: Prompt is instructions. RAG is knowledge. Tools are live data and actions. Fine-tuning is behavior. Pick by what is missing.
